   CITY OF LA VERNE

  PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
  MEETING AGENDA

  Wednesday, December 8, 2021, 9:00 a.m.
  Watch Live at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream
  3660 D Street, La Verne, CA 91750

The Public Financing Authority meeting for La Verne’s Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District will
be closed to the public in compliance with Governor Newsom’s Executive Order to minimize the
spread of the COVID-19 Virus. However, the public is encouraged to participate in this meeting in
any of the following ways:

  1) View the meeting through the City’s website at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream
  2) Please submit your written comments via email at planning@cityoflaverne.org. They will be
  shared with the Authority Members prior to the meeting and will be made part of the
  permanent record. We ask that you provide those emails before 7:00 p.m. the day before the
  meeting. Please be advised that public comments submitted by emails or any other
  format to the City are public records that will be made available for public viewing.
  3) Participate on Zoom by registering here before 8:00 am the day of the meeting:
  https://us02web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_f2Htp84tTUGvqIPzkvq_NA
  4) For individuals that wish to share their comments during the live stream, you may email
  planning@cityoflaverne.org by 8:00 a.m. on the day of the meeting with a phone number and
  the item(s) you wish to speak on. We will call you back at the appropriate time during the
  meeting for your comment.

In compliance with the American Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires a
modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Assistant City
Clerk’s Office at (909) 596-8726 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

1.  CALL TO ORDER

  Board Members:  Supervisor Kathryn Barger, Chair, Elected Member
  Robin Carder, Vice Chair, Elected Member
  Mayor Tim Hepburn, Elected Member
  Raymond Skelton, Member of the Public
  Vacant, Member of the Public

  Staff:  Robert Russi, City Manager
  Eric Scherer, Director of Community Development
  Lupe Gaeta Estrella, Assistant City Clerk
 2.  Approval of Minutes – June 9, 2021 and September 29, 2021

3.  Declaration of Emergency - Pursuant to Government Code Section 54953, the Public
  Financing Authority may continue to hold their public meetings via teleconference due to the
  COVID-19 pandemic by adopting a resolution. Staff has prepared a resolution declaring the
  need to continue to meet teleconferencing at this time.

  Staff recommends that the Authority Board approve PFA Resolution No. 21-1 allowing for
  meetings to occur via teleconference.

4.  Pedestrian Bridge Design Update – Staff will present an update to the Authority Board on the
  planned Pedestrian Bridge from the L Line Station Plaza to the Fairplex campus.

  No action is required by the Authority Board.

5.  Street Improvements Update – Staff will provide the Authority Board of the status of design
  work underway for street and pedestrian improvements from the L Line Station Plaza to Old
  Town La Verne.

  No action is required by the Authority Board.

6.  L Line and Development Updates – Staff will update the Authority Board on the progress of
  construction of the L Line and private development within or near the District.

  No action is required by the Authority Board.

7.  PUBLIC COMMENTS/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS - This is the time set aside for anyone
  wishing to address the Public Financing Authority on items not listed in any other place on the
  agenda. Under the provisions of the Brown Act, the legislative body is prohibited from talking or
  engaging in discussion on any item not appearing on the posted agenda. However, your
  concerns may be referred to staff or set for discussion at a later date. The Chair reserves the
  right to place limits on duration of comments.

8.  ADJOURNMENT – The next regularly scheduled meeting of the Public Financing Authority will
  be held on Wednesday, March 9, 2022 at 9:00 a.m., and is expected to be held virtually at
  www.cityoflaverne.org/stream
   LA VERNE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
  Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District (EIFD)
  Minutes of a Regular Meeting
  Wednesday, June 9, 2021
  Teleconference
  ___________________________________________

1.  The Public Financing Authority meeting for La Verne’s Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District
  was closed to the public in compliance with Governor Newsom’s Executive Order to minimize the
  spread of the COVID-19 Virus. Additionally, the meeting was conducted via teleconference with
  all Authority members and members of the public participating remotely.

2.  A regular meeting of the La Verne Public Financing Authority was called to order by Vice- Chair
  Carder at 9:02 a.m.

3.  Board Members Present: Mayor Tim Hepburn, Vice-Chair Robin Carder, Raymond Skelton, and
  Gilbert Ivey.

  Board Member Absent: Chair Los Angeles County Supervisor Barger.

  Staff Present: Executive Director Robert Russi, and Community Development Director Eric
  Scherer.

4.  La Verne Public Financing  It was moved by Ivey, seconded by Hepburn, and carried by a
  Authority Enhanced  roll call vote of 4-0 (Barger absent) to approve the La Verne
  Infrastructure Financing District  Public Financing Authority Enhanced Infrastructure Financing
  (EIFD) Minutes  District (EIFD) Minutes of March 3, 2021

5.  Infrastructure and Facility  Community Development Director Scherer reported on the
  Reimbursement Agreement  Infrastructure and Facility Reimbursement Agreement. He
  stated that the Public Financing Authority Board at their March
  3, 2021 meeting heard and discussed the proposed financing
  options to implement the initial projects listed in the
  Infrastructure Financing Plan. Based on direction and input by
  the City Council, the Board directed staff to prepare an
  agreement that would have the City provide the initial funds
  with a repayment component. At their May 17, 2021 meeting,
  the City Council approved the draft Infrastructure and Facility
  Reimbursement Agreement, pending approval by the Board.

  City Manager Russi stated that the Reimbursement Agreement
  is similar to the ones that were done when the La Verne
  Redevelopment Agency existed. He reported that quarterly
  reports would be submitted to the Board on the progress and
  funding of the proposed projects.

  Vice-Chair Carder called for public comment on this matter.

  There was none.

  It was moved by Hepburn, seconded by Skelton, and carried by
  a roll call vote of 4-0 (Barger absent) to approve PFA Resolution
  No. 21-02 approving the Infrastructure and Facility
  Reimbursement Agreement.
 Public Financing Authority Minutes (EIFD), Wednesday, June 9, 2021, page 2

  6.  First Annual Report of the  Community Development Director Scherer reported on first
  Enhanced Infrastructure  annual report of the Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District
  Financing District (EIFD)  (EIFD). He stated that per State Law, the Public Financing
  Authority is required to adopt an annual report of activities
  undertaken within the last fiscal year. This is the first annual
  report of the District, and it was mailed out to all property
  owners and participating taxing entities (County). He reported
  there was no contact from the property owners or agencies
  regarding the annual report.

  Vice-Chair Carder called for public comment on this matter.

  There was none.

  It was moved by Ivey, seconded by Hepburn, and carried by a
  roll call vote of 4-0 (Barger absent) to approve PFA Resolution
  No. 21-03, adopting the submitted Annual Report for fiscal year
  2020-2021.

 7.  Public Comment  PUBLIC COMMENTS/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS - This is
  the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the
  La Verne Financing Authority on items not listed in any other
  place on the agenda. Under the provisions of the Brown
  Act, the legislative body is prohibited from talking or
  engaging in discussion on any item not appearing on the
  posted agenda. However, your concerns may be referred to
  staff or set for discussion at a later date. Any people desiring
  to speak were asked to email their comments prior to the close
  of the public comment period including their name and address
  for the record. The Chair reserves the right to place limits on
  duration of comments.

  Vice Chair Carder called for public comment

  There was none.

  City Manager Russi reported that Congress Member Grace
  Napolitano has earmarked one million dollars towards the
  construction of the puddingstone pedestrian bridge.

  Vice Chair Carder spoke about the proposed Carvana Used
  Car dealership at the Fairplex and its proximity to the Arrow
  Highway pedestrian bridge.

  City Manager Russi stated that the Arrow Highway pedestrian
  bridge would connect to the La Verne Gold Line Station
  spanning to the northern edge of the Fairplex property.

  Mayor Hepburn spoke about the partnerships involved helping
  to build the pedestrian bridge. He stated he really appreciated
  and thanked City Manager Russi and City staff for their work on
  this matter.

  Board Members Skelton stated that it’s an exciting process.
 Public Financing Authority Minutes (EIFD), Wednesday, June 9, 2021, page 2

  Board Member Ivey stated he is very supportive of the project.

  8.  Meeting adjourned at the next regularly scheduled meeting of the Public Financing Authority will be
  held on Wednesday, September 8, 2021, and is expected to be held virtually at
  www.cityoflaverne.org/stream.

  Respectfully submitted,

  Lupe Gaeta Estrella, CMC
  Secretary/Assistant City Clerk

   PFA RESOLUTION NO. 21-1

A RESOLUTION OF THE LA VERNE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY (PFA)
FORMING ENHANCED INFRASTRUCTURE FINANCING DISTRICT NO.1 MAKING
SPECIFIED FINDINGS TO ENABLE THE PFA TO CONTINUE TO HOLD MEETINGS
VIA TELECONFERENCING

  WHEREAS, AB 361 (Rivas), and specifically Government Code section 54953
(“Section 54953”), authorizes local agencies to use teleconferencing without complying
with the specified teleconferencing requirements imposed by the Ralph M. Brown Act
when the legislative body of a local agency holds a meeting during a declared state of
emergency and makes certain findings relating thereto; and

  WHEREAS, Section 54953 allows for local agencies to teleconference if the
legislative body finds, among other things, that state or local official continue to impose
or recommend measures to promote social distancing or whether a state of emergency
directly impacts the ability of the legislative body to meet safely and that meeting in
person would present imminent risks to the health and safety of attendees; and

  WHEREAS, on March 4, 2020, the Governor of California proclaimed a State of
Emergency to exist in California as result of the threat of COVID-19, which state of
emergency remains in place; and

  WHEREAS, on March 4, 2020, the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors
and Los Angeles County Health Officer declared a local and health emergency as result
of the threat of COVID-19, which emergency remains in place; and

  WHEREAS, Los Angeles County and State health officials continue to
recommend social distancing as a result of COVID-19; and

  WHEREAS, due to the resurgence of COVID-19 reported cases and surge of the
Delta variant statewide and in particular, in Los Angeles County, the California
Department of Public Health’s Best Practice Guidance encourages all governmental
entities to refrain from conducting indoor meetings and consider moving operations
outdoors, where feasible, in order to prevent transmission; and

  WHEREAS, teleconferencing meetings enables the PFA to retain the ability to
continue to conduct meetings in a safe manner that would reduce exposure to members
and staff to COVID-19; and

  WHEREAS, public access and participation remain a core value of the PFA, and
the PFA has the capability to meet the requirements in Section 54953 to provide the
public with the ability to view, hear, and participate in such meetings in a manner that
protects the statutory and constitutional rights of all persons to participate in such
meetings; and
   WHEREAS, as a condition of extending the use of the provisions to conduct
remote teleconference meetings without compliance with specified Brown Act
teleconference requirements, the PFA must reconsider the circumstances of the state of
emergency that exists, and the PFA Board has done so.

  NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the PFA Board does hereby find
the existence of a local and state of emergency in California caused by COVID-19
continues to directly impact the ability of the PFA to hold public meetings safely in
person and local and state health officials continue to recommend social distancing.

  PASSED, APPROVED, and ADOPTED by the Public Financing Authority Board
of the City of La Verne’s Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District No. 1, on December
8, 2021 by the following vote:
